title: iAccess Partners and QAI Ventures Partner to Lower Entry Threshold for Early-Stage Quantum VC Fund - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Swiss fintech iAccess Partners and Basel VC firm QAI Ventures partnered to use bankable ISINs to cut the minimum ticket for early-stage quantum and deep-tech venture investing to USD $25,000, opening pre-seed/seed quantum, sensing, communications, and HPC/semiconductor deal flow to smaller qualified investors who previously needed institutional-scale commitments.

themes.theme: Structural access mechanism for deep-tech VC

insights.claim: iAccess Partners and QAI Ventures use bankable International Securities Identification Numbers (ISINs) to let qualified and professional investors access early-stage quantum technology venture investments through standard bank custody accounts for a minimum commitment of USD $25,000.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A $25,000 minimum via a bankable ISIN structure materially lowers the capital bar for quantum venture exposure, opening a previously institution-only asset class to wealth-management clients and smaller professional investors.

insights.claim: Venture investments in early-stage deep-tech companies have historically been restricted to large institutional investors such as pension funds and insurance companies due to high minimum capital commitments and complex private equity subscription paperwork.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Names the specific structural barrier (subscription paperwork and institutional-scale minimums) this product is designed to remove, framing this deal as part of a broader trend of deep-tech VC 'democratization' via digital wrapper structures.

insights.claim: The digital bankable ISIN structure lets qualified private investors, wealth managers, and financial intermediaries execute quantum-sector venture investments via standard bank custody accounts with fully digital onboarding, bypassing complex private equity subscription paperwork.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is a repeatable fintech wrapper model (ISIN + bank custody + digital onboarding) that could be applied by other VC firms in adjacent deep-tech sectors, worth tracking as a template for retail/semi-retail access to venture asset classes.

insights.claim: Capital raised through the partnership will feed into QAI Ventures' latest fund, which targets early-stage (pre-seed and seed) startups in quantum processors, quantum sensors, quantum encryption, high-performance computing (HPC), and next-generation semiconductors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The fund's scope spans quantum hardware plus adjacent HPC and semiconductor plays, meaning this is effectively broad deep-tech infrastructure exposure branded as a quantum fund -- relevant for investors assessing true sector concentration.
insights.locator: 'Focus on Pre-Seed and Seed Stages' bullet

insights.claim: QAI Ventures sources deal flow through its own global accelerator hubs operating across Switzerland, Canada, Singapore, and Japan, and the firm's portfolio already includes more than 35 companies.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 35+ company portfolio sourced from four international accelerator hubs gives QAI Ventures meaningful existing pipeline breadth, a concrete scale marker for evaluating this as an established rather than nascent quantum VC platform.

insights.claim: QAI Ventures CEO and General Partner Alexandra Beckstein said expert scientific diligence is essential in quantum market selection and that structured investment platforms let smaller-ticket investors participate directly in foundational economic infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals QAI Ventures is positioning quantum technology as 'foundational economic infrastructure' comparable to other infrastructure asset classes, a framing investors can use to gauge how the firm pitches quantum risk to newer capital sources.
